quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: When you see a steady green light, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, let pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection pass first. You can drive through, but slow down in case the light changes before you reach the intersection.

questions.question: When you are in a travel lane on the road, what should you do?

options.text: You can stop to drop off passengers.
You can stop to look up an address.
You can make a U-turn or back up if you take the wrong freeway entrance.
Don't stop. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't stop. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane for any reason. Keep moving until you reach a safe spot to pull off. If you miss your exit, go to the next one instead of backing up.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Call the police right away.
Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show you disagree.
Do something aggressive back to them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get away from them. Do not try to get revenge, as this makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Hazard flashers.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams bounce off the fog and reflect back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What does a steady green light mean?

options.text: You must slow down and be ready to stop.
You must stop and check for traffic before going.
You can drive through if the road is clear.
You cannot turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can drive through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through the intersection if it is safe. You can also turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. Always let other vehicles and pedestrians pass first.

questions.question: At an intersection with no signs or signals, you arrive at the same time as a car on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross first.
Slow down and let the car on your right go.
Drive into the intersection and make them stop.
Honk and drive through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the car on your right go.
questions.explanation: When two cars arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the car on the right has the right-of-way. Let them pass first.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: Slow down.
Look for a train.
Be ready to stop.
Do all of the above.

questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If warning lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not try to go around the gate.

questions.question: When a driver enters the road from a driveway or private road, what should they do?

options.text: They have the right-of-way.
They should let drivers on the road go first.
They can force their way into traffic.
Other drivers will move to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should let drivers on the road go first.
questions.explanation: When entering the road from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the road. Merge safely when you have a clear space.

questions.question: When you see an aggressive driver, what should you do?

options.text: Don't make eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Tailgate them to get back at them.
Make sure they know you disapprove.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't make eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If another driver is driving dangerously near you, stay calm and create distance. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: When is it important to slow down?

options.text: On narrow or winding roads.
At intersections or railroad crossings.
When the road is wet or slippery.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, at intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp curves, near pedestrians, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention while driving
Driving too fast for the conditions
Following other vehicles too closely
All of the above

questions.explanation: Driving too fast causes crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: What substances can impair your driving ability and cause a DUII arrest?

options.text: Beer, wine, and liquor
Illegal drugs or prescription medicines
Inhalants like glue or paint
All of the above

questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include all alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medications including prescription and over-the-counter drugs.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal before you change lanes.
Check your blind spot.
Make sure the lane is clear first.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes or exiting. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get away from it.
Stop immediately and block its path.
Give it a clear path to travel.
Signal when it is safe for it to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give it a clear path to travel.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, give it a clear path. Pull to the side of the road if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Highway hypnosis happens when:

options.text: You stare at the road for a long time.
You take frequent rest stops.
You sleep too much before driving.
You take short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: You stare at the road for a long time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead without looking around. This causes you to lose focus and may cause you to crash into stopped traffic ahead.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Avoid standing water and puddles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, cars take longer to stop and may skid during quick turns. Do not use cruise control on wet or icy roads. Slow down and drive with care.

questions.question: When stopped by police, a driver must show:

options.text: Proof of insurance.
Their driver's license.
Proof of registration.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Drivers must have and show their license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance when stopped. All three are required in your vehicle at all times.

questions.question: What helps someone recover from drinking alcohol?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime
Hot coffee
Fresh air
Only time

questions.explanation: Only time will help alcohol leave your body.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No left turn.
Flagger ahead.
Two-way left turn.
Turn right or go through.

questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers what they must do. It means you cannot turn left.

questions.question: You should always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, parking, or pulling into traffic. Let other drivers know what you are doing to prevent accidents.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the accident.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at or near the accident scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes — another vehicle could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never put an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can hurt an infant or small child, even in a low-speed crash.
Always make sure all passengers use a seat belt or child restraint.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Fasten your seat belt before you drive. Make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your chance of injury or death in a crash. Children 12 and under should sit in the back seat with proper restraints. Never put a rear-facing infant seat in the front seat of a vehicle with a front airbag.

questions.question: Where is passing prohibited?

options.text: On hills and curves.
At intersections.
At railroad crossings.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not pass another vehicle on hills, curves, at intersections, or at railroad crossings. These areas are unsafe and illegal for passing.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No left turn.
No U-turns.
No exit.
No right turn.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: What is the correct order of traffic lights from top to bottom?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.
Green, yellow, red.

questions.explanation: Red is always on top and green on the bottom on a vertical traffic light. On a horizontal light, red is on the left and green is on the right.

questions.question: What should you do to prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread.
Keep your tires properly inflated.
Slow down when driving in rain.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, your tires must have good tread and be inflated to the correct pressure. Slow down when driving in rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at higher speeds.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver who arrives first.
The driver who arrives last.
One driver should continue without stopping.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.explanation: All four drivers must stop at a four-way stop. The driver who arrives first goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar car from a friend. What should you do?

options.text: Do not worry — all cars are the same.
Do not tell your friend you are unfamiliar with the car.
Ignore any obvious problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn where the controls are and how they work before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where the controls are and how they work before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar car, spend a few minutes learning the location and use of the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, wipers, brakes, gear shift, and horn. Fix any problems before driving.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger tells you to stop.
When there is a stop sign.
When flashing red lights and gates are present and working.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing if a flagger signals you to stop, if there is a stop sign, or if flashing red lights and gates are working.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It improves driving skills but harms judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It does not affect driving skills or judgment.
It harms judgment but improves driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms skills needed for safe driving, including reaction time and vision. It also affects your judgment about speed and distance, lowers your caution, and makes you take more risks.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
Take the right-of-way.
Proceed normally.
Drive away quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: You may use this lane.
No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You have the right-of-way.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.explanation: A steady green arrow pointing down means you can use that lane.

questions.question: When a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Copy what other cars are doing, even if the guard says otherwise.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Always obey a crossing guard's directions in a school zone. Slow down and use extra caution when a guard or police officer tells you to do so.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, what should you do?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Come to a complete stop.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of danger ahead. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol will help the medicine cure a cold.
The effects of the alcohol or medicine can become much stronger.
There is no effect because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of the alcohol or medicine can become much stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with medicine can strengthen the effects of both. For example, one drink while taking a cold medicine could affect you like several drinks would on their own.
